neighbours.label: judging an offer as too good: ' too' after 'seems', 'looks', 'sounds' about a deal or prize, and gain with no effort
fire: That offer seems too cheap to be real.
The prize looked too big to be honest.
This deal sounds too easy to believe.
The job looked too simple to be safe.
Win a new phone with no effort required!
Make fast money with no risk at all!
That loan seems too generous to trust.
Get free cash with no work at all!
quiet: That box seems rather cheap and plain.
The prize looked quite big and shiny.
This road sounds very long to walk.
The soup was too hot to eat.
Win a new phone by solving the quiz.
Make fresh bread with flour and water.
That loan seems fair and clear.
The car is too old to sell.

short: offer seeming too good, effortless gain
notes: Second round; the first ('too good to be true, easy gain') failed because ' too' in 'looked too small', 'seems too hot' and 'sounds too long' fired. New probes: 'too small to be useful' and 'too hot to go outside' after is/was 0.02-0.05; 'no effort' 0.74; 'easy money' 0.42. So the evaluation verb looks like what matters. Two near misses keep ' too' after is/was.
